memoryBlocks._whyDocumented: The .bss block is not optional. It has no bytes in the ROM, so Ghidra has no memory there unless it is created. Every global living in bss then resolves to an address Ghidra reports as nonexistent, and a structure query returns ZERO HITS — which reads as 'nothing accesses this field' rather than 'this address is not mapped'. That misdiagnosis cost three attempts.

textualAddressSearchDoesNotWorkOnARM.detail: A search for the literal text of a bss address in instruction operands found 0 hits across 150,278 instructions, while the reference database found 6 real cross-references to the same address. ARM does not encode a global address in the instruction — it loads it from a LITERAL POOL (LDR rX, [pc, #N]; ... .word 0x021974dc). So 'which code touches this global' must be answered from resolved references, not from scanning instruction text. A textual scan produces a confident, wrong 'nothing accesses this'.
textualAddressSearchDoesNotWorkOnARM.consequence: Use OgaXrefsTo (reference database), not OgaSearchOffset (operand scan), to find the users of a global.

openQuestions.detail: Three of the six gForces readers are still auto-named. FUN_02040094 reads the array twice, which suggests a two-faction loop (player/enemy) — the decomp has `for (forceId = 0; forceId < 2; forceId++)` in ov000/map_sequence.cpp:2474, so this is a likely match but NOT confirmed.
